attachments.text:
This cold email got 43 replies.

It was sent to supermarket owners.
B2C, solar panels, parking lots.

But the magic?
It works in B2B too.
Because it’s not about the product.

It’s about the framework.

Here’s the breakdown anyone can steal:

Subject:
“your parking”
Looks like an internal note. Boring works.

Hook:
“I visited your supermarket and noticed…”
Personal, relevant, rooted in reality.

Problem:
“A new law requires solar canopies…”
Urgent. External. Not made up.

CTA:
“Have you already contracted a provider?”
No demo. No friction. Just a simple yes/no.

Social proof:
“Here’s how Costco handled it.”
Adds trust. No bragging.

Now imagine you’re selling B2B SaaS.

Same structure:

• Subject: “your pricing page”
• Hook: “I noticed you don’t capture intent signals”
• Problem: “Most SaaS lose 30% of leads at this stage”
• CTA: “Worth a quick chat to fix it?”
• Social proof: “X company increased signups by 40%”

You don’t need tricks.
You don’t need clever copy.
You need a real reason to reach out and a structure that respects people’s time.

This works in any industry.
Any vertical. Any offer.

Want replies?

Make it feel like a conversation, not a pitch.

Have you tried this kind of structure before? | 30 comments on LinkedIn
